items.title: CISA Warns of Check Point 0-Day Vulnerability Exploited to Gain Root Access
items.summary: CISA has warned that attackers are exploiting a Check Point security flaw that lets a local user gain root access on affected appliances. The agency added CVE-2026-123039 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on November 13, 2026, confirming that the vulnerability is being used in real attacks. Check Point said it observed exploitation against “a couple of dozen customers.” The flaw carries a CVSS score of 7.8 and affects the DynamicCLI service in Gaia OS. Successful exploitation allows commands to run with the highest operating system rights, putting affected firewalls and management systems at risk. Check Point Root Access Vulnerability The weakness sits in dynamic_server , a process that runs as root and handles extended command-line functions. It receives requests through /tmp/dynamic_socket , a local communication socket. On vulnerable systems, this socket has permissions set to 0777 , allowing any local user to write to it without proper access restrictions. The service also fails to authenticate the process sending a request. It executes the received command as root, turning limited local access into full system control. However, this is not a standalone remote code execution flaw. An attacker must already have local code execution on the appliance before exploiting it. Cybersecurity News previously covered Check Point firewall attacks involving PHP2Shell , where attackers used this privilege escalation flaw after gaining initial access. That distinction matters because fixing an entry point alone does not remove every weakness attackers could use after reaching a device or gaining a service account. Affected Products and Available Fixes According to Check Point’s security advisory , affected products include Force Firewalls, Management and Log Servers, Multi-Domain management and logging systems, and Maestro Orchestrator. Vulnerable releases span R81, R81.10, R81.20, R82, R82.10, and R82.20. Check Point Spark Firewalls and Smart-1 Cloud are not affected by this flaw. Check Point has released fixes in Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator updates. Protected releases start at R82.20 Take 14, R82.10 Take 52, R82 Take 132, and R81.20 Take 174. The correction blocks and logs unauthorized DynamicCLI requests. R81 and R81.10 are listed as end-of-support versions in the advisory. For temporary mitigation, administrators can stop the service and prevent its restart by running dbset process:dynamic_server , followed by dbset :save . Check Point warns that this disables the Dynamic CLI commands described in its documentation. Administrators should account for that operational impact rather than treating the workaround as a permanent replacement for patching. The daemon records received commands in /var/log/dynamicCli.log . Requests that lack the expected Clish wrapper need investigation. Check Point also recommends checking for unusual commands involving account creation, SSH keys, downloads, or sensitive files. After patching, /tmp/dynamic_socket should show permissions of 0660 , owned by root and the config group, rather than 0777 . Earlier Check Point VPN zero-day coverage showed how gateway flaws can expose sensitive information. This case requires local access, but confirmed exploitation makes patching and compromise checks urgent. CISA’s alert urges organizations to prioritize known exploited vulnerabilities. items.title: Uber Confirms Data Breach – Hackers Stole Users’ Personal Information
items.summary: Uber has confirmed a data breach involving the personal information of thousands of U.S. drivers after hackers accessed records held by Fireworks AI, a third-party technology provider. The exposed information includes driver’s license details. Uber is notifying affected people, but it has not disclosed the total number impacted nationwide. The incident became known to Uber on October 9, 2026, when its service provider reported that an unauthorized party had compromised internal login credentials. Those credentials allowed the attacker to access Uber’s account with the provider, creating a path to personal records stored outside Uber’s own systems. Uber said it immediately cut its data connections with the provider and opened an investigation. On October 13, investigators confirmed that the attacker had accessed Uber data, including personal information belonging to people now receiving breach notices. The notification letter is dated November 10, 2026. Stolen Credentials Exposed Driver Records State notices show that the breach affected 2,567 people in Massachusetts, 3,430 in South Carolina, and approximately 1,873 in Rhode Island. Together, those figures cover 7,870 people across three states. Additional notifications involve other states, meaning this count does not represent the full scale of the breach. The public California notice leaves the exposed data fields blank rather than listing specific information. However, state filings reviewed by TechCrunch identified driver’s license information among the stolen records. The available evidence concerns drivers and should not be read as confirmation that all Uber riders or accounts were affected. An Uber spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch that Fireworks AI was the vendor involved. Cyber Security News previously covered the wider Fireworks AI data breach , which exposed customer records and some datasets. However, those broader findings do not establish which additional data, if any, belonged to Uber. The same provider also handled data involved in the Notion AI chat transcript breach . Notion said fewer than 1% of customer workspaces were affected and that its own systems were not breached. These separate disclosures show how one provider’s security incident can expose information belonging to several customers. Protection for Affected Drivers Uber’s official breach notice says it had not identified misuse of the affected information when the letter was issued. The company is offering free credit monitoring and fraud assistance through Cyberscout, a TransUnion company. Recipients must enroll within 90 days of the letter’s date using their activation code. Affected drivers should review their individual letters, check account statements, and report suspicious activity. Uber also recommends considering fraud alerts or credit freezes. The Federal Trade Commission explains that a credit freeze limits access to credit reports, making fraudulent new accounts harder to open.
